referenceMaterial.content:
# Instruction fields the decoder reads

Source for the `ctrl_decode` block of the RV32I demo. Hand-transcribed from the RISC-V
Unprivileged ISA, RV32I base instruction set; check against the ratified specification
before relying on it.

## Opcode

Bits 6:0 of the instruction word, as a 7-bit binary value:

| opcode | instruction class |
|---|---|
| 0110111 | upper-immediate load (LUI) |
| 0010111 | upper-immediate plus pc (AUIPC) |
| 1101111 | direct jump and link (JAL) |
| 1100111 | register jump and link (JALR) |
| 1100011 | conditional branch |
| 0000011 | load |
| 0100011 | store |
| 0010011 | register-immediate arithmetic |
| 0110011 | register-register arithmetic |

Any other opcode is not an instruction this decoder recognises.

## funct3

Bits 14:12. It is a function code only under the opcodes listed in this section.
For the upper-immediate loads (0110111, 0010111) and the direct jump (1101111) these
bits are part of the immediate and carry no meaning of their own.

### Register jump and link (opcode 1100111)

| funct3 | meaning |
|---|---|
| 000 | register jump and link |

Any other funct3 is not a register jump and link.

### Conditional branch (opcode 1100011)

| funct3 | condition |
|---|---|
| 000 | equal |
| 001 | not equal |
| 100 | less than |
| 101 | greater or equal |
| 110 | less than, unsigned |
| 111 | greater or equal, unsigned |

010 and 011 are not branches.

### Load (opcode 0000011)

| funct3 | access |
|---|---|
| 000 | byte |
| 001 | half |
| 010 | word |
| 100 | byte, unsigned |
| 101 | half, unsigned |

011, 110 and 111 are not loads.

### Store (opcode 0100011)

| funct3 | access |
|---|---|
| 000 | byte |
| 001 | half |
| 010 | word |

All other values are not stores.

### Arithmetic (opcodes 0010011 and 0110011)

| funct3 | operation |
|---|---|
| 000 | add (subtract when bit 30 is 1, register-register form only) |
| 001 | shift left |
| 010 | set less than |
| 011 | set less than, unsigned |
| 100 | xor |
| 101 | shift right (arithmetic when bit 30 is 1) |
| 110 | or |
| 111 | and |

For register-immediate arithmetic, bit 30 matters only for funct3 101.

Bit 30 of the instruction word is read only where this table says so (subtract, and
arithmetic shift right). Under any other funct3 it is ignored: it does not change
the operation and does not make the instruction unrecognised.

## Combinations not listed

An opcode that is listed with funct3 values, paired with a funct3 value that is not
listed for it, is not a recognised instruction, whatever the opcode's class would
otherwise suggest. For example: a store with funct3 011, a branch with funct3 010, a
load with funct3 111.

blocks.name: pc
blocks.description: Fetch-stage program counter. Holds the address of the instruction being fetched, always a multiple of two. On each rising clock edge, in this order: when rst is 1 the held address becomes 80000000 hexadecimal, the first address of RAM; otherwise when trap_redirect is 1 it becomes trap_pc; otherwise when redirect is 1 it becomes redirect_pc; otherwise when stall is 1 it is left unchanged; otherwise it becomes the held address plus two when is16 is 1 and plus four when is16 is 0. trap_redirect comes from the write-back stage (an exception, an interrupt or mret) and so is older than redirect, which comes from the execute stage: when both are 1 the older one wins. is16 is 1 when the instruction being fetched is a 16-bit compressed instruction. pc is the held address. pc_plus4 is the address of the instruction after the one being fetched: the held address plus two when is16 is 1 and plus four when is16 is 0 (wrapping at 32 bits), available without waiting for a clock edge. trap_pc and redirect_pc are full 32-bit addresses and are loaded as they are, except that bit 0 of what is loaded is 0.

blocks.name: imem
blocks.description: Instruction memory. Words the file does not set read as zero.

blocks.name: if_id
blocks.description: IF/ID pipeline register. Sits between the fetch stage and the decode stage. Every output shows the value its matching input had at the last rising clock edge; nothing changes between edges, and no output depends combinationally on any input. On each rising clock edge: when rst is 1 or flush is 1, the register is cleared: pc_out becomes 0; pc_plus4_out becomes 0; inst_out becomes 32'h00000013, the instruction addi x0, x0, 0, which changes nothing (a bubble). Otherwise, when stall is 1, every output keeps its value. Otherwise every output takes the value of its matching input. A flush is how the instruction fetched on a wrong path is turned into a bubble. A further output, valid_out, is 0 after the register has been cleared (reset or flush) and becomes 1 at the first rising edge on which the register is loaded from its inputs (not cleared and not held); while stall holds the register, valid_out keeps its value. It tells the later stages that the instruction in this register is a real one and not a bubble.

blocks.name: ctrl_decode
blocks.description: Combinational instruction decoder. Reads the 32-bit instruction word and drives every control signal in the design, plus the three register selector fields. The register selectors are plain slices of the instruction: rs1 is bits 19:15, rs2 is bits 24:20 and rd is bits 11:7. Every control output's meaning is given by its own encoding table; decode the instruction's opcode field (bits 6:0), funct3 field (bits 14:12) and bit 30 and drive each control output to the code that matches. Most instruction words are not valid instructions, so the unrecognised case is not an edge case: an instruction the decoder does not recognise must drive regwrite to NO_WRITE, memwrite to NO_STORE, brsel to NO_BRANCH, pcsel to NEXT and memtype to NO_ACCESS, so that it changes no architectural state and touches no memory. For an unrecognised instruction immsel, memsrc, alusrc, arith and opsel are don't care: with nothing written and no jump taken, nothing reads them. An opcode alone does not make an instruction valid. For an opcode whose funct3 values are listed (branch, load, store, the two arithmetic opcodes, and the register jump, whose only listed value is 000), a funct3 value that is not listed for it (a store with a width code that is not byte, half or word, for example) makes the instruction unrecognised, and the unrecognised case above applies, not the values the opcode's class would give. For the upper-immediate loads and the direct jump, bits 14:12 are part of the immediate, not a function code: they never make the instruction unrecognised, and the outputs do not depend on them. Bit 30 of the instruction word is read only where the funct3 table says so (subtract, and arithmetic shift right); under any other funct3 it is ignored and never makes an instruction unrecognised. The arithmetic unit's result is consumed in only three places: written back when memsrc is FROM_ALU, used as a data memory address, and used as the jump target for JUMPREG. An instruction that uses none of the three (a conditional branch, which compares through the branch comparator, an upper-immediate load, and a direct jump) does not use the arithmetic unit, so for it alusrc, arith and opsel are don't care. The add-upper-immediate-to-pc instruction (opcode 0010111) is not an upper-immediate load: what it writes back is the address plus the immediate, computed by the arithmetic unit, so it does use the arithmetic unit, writes back FROM_ALU, and takes the immediate as its second operand. The register jump and link writes back the link address, the current address plus four, so it writes back FROM_PC; its jump target is the first register plus the immediate, computed by the arithmetic unit, so it also uses the arithmetic unit and takes the immediate as its second operand. The arithmetic unit's first operand is the register value for rs1, except for the add-upper-immediate-to-pc instruction, whose first operand is the address of the instruction itself: asel is USE_PC for that instruction and USE_REGISTER for every other instruction that uses the arithmetic unit; where the arithmetic unit is not used asel is don't care. No clock, no reset, no state.

semantics.description: Whether this instruction writes a result back to a register.

encoding.0: NO_WRITE: the register file is left unchanged
encoding.1: WRITE: wdata is stored into the register selected by waddr

semantics.description: Which value is used as the arithmetic unit's second operand.

encoding.0: USE_REGISTER: the second operand is b_reg
encoding.1: USE_IMMEDIATE: the second operand is b_imm

semantics.description: Modifies two of the operation codes, mirroring how a real instruction set reuses one code for two related operations. Every other operation ignores it, and arith is 0 for those.

encoding.0: LOGICAL: SHIFT_RIGHT shifts in zeros, and ADD_SUB adds
encoding.1: ARITHMETIC: SHIFT_RIGHT replicates the sign bit, and ADD_SUB subtracts

semantics.description: Which operation the arithmetic unit applies to its two operands.

encoding.000: ADD_SUB: adds the operands, or subtracts the second from the first when arith is 1; the result wraps on overflow
encoding.001: SHIFT_LEFT: the first operand shifted left by the low five bits of the second, zeros shifted in
encoding.010: SET_LESS_THAN: 1 when the first operand is less than the second, both read as signed two's complement, otherwise 0
encoding.011: SET_LESS_THAN_UNSIGNED: 1 when the first operand is less than the second, both read as unsigned, otherwise 0
encoding.100: XOR: bitwise exclusive or of the operands
encoding.101: SHIFT_RIGHT: the first operand shifted right by the low five bits of the second; zeros shifted in when arith is 0, the sign bit replicated when arith is 1
encoding.110: OR: bitwise or of the operands
encoding.111: AND: bitwise and of the operands

semantics.description: Which immediate layout to extract from the instruction word, and how to extend it to 32 bits.

encoding.000: IMM_I: bits 31:20 of the instruction, sign-extended
encoding.001: IMM_S: bits 31:25 concatenated with bits 11:7, sign-extended
encoding.010: IMM_B: bit 31, bit 7, bits 30:25, bits 11:8, then a zero bit, sign-extended
encoding.011: IMM_U: bits 31:12 placed in the upper 20 bits, the low 12 bits zero
encoding.100: IMM_J: bit 31, bits 19:12, bit 20, bits 30:21, then a zero bit, sign-extended
encoding.101: NO_IMMEDIATE: the output is zero; this instruction has no immediate operand, and this is the code for it

semantics.description: Which comparison decides whether a branch is taken.

encoding.000: BR_EQ: taken when the operands are equal
encoding.001: BR_NE: taken when the operands differ
encoding.010: BR_LT: taken when the first is less than the second, both signed
encoding.011: BR_GE: taken when the first is greater than or equal to the second, both signed
encoding.100: BR_LTU: taken when the first is less than the second, both unsigned
encoding.101: BR_GEU: taken when the first is greater than or equal to the second, both unsigned
encoding.111: NO_BRANCH: never taken; this instruction is not a branch

semantics.description: The width and extension of a data memory access.

encoding.000: MEM_BYTE: one byte, sign-extended to 32 bits
encoding.001: MEM_HALF: two bytes, sign-extended to 32 bits
encoding.011: MEM_BYTE_U: one byte, zero-extended to 32 bits
encoding.100: MEM_HALF_U: two bytes, zero-extended to 32 bits
encoding.101: NO_ACCESS: behaves as MEM_WORD; this instruction does not access data memory, and this is the code for it

semantics.description: Whether this instruction stores to data memory.

encoding.0: NO_STORE: memory is left unchanged
encoding.1: STORE: wdata is written at addr, in the width memtype selects

semantics.description: Which value is written back to the register file.

encoding.01: FROM_MEMORY: the value read from data memory
encoding.10: FROM_PC: the current address plus four, for a call
encoding.11: FROM_IMMEDIATE: the immediate, for an upper-immediate instruction

semantics.description: How the next program counter is chosen at the end of this instruction.

encoding.00: NEXT: the next address is the current address plus four
encoding.01: BRANCH: the next address is the current address plus imm when taken is 1, otherwise the current address plus four
encoding.10: JUMP: the next address is the current address plus imm, unconditionally
encoding.11: JUMPREG: the next address is jump_addr with its lowest bit forced to 0

semantics.description: Which value the arithmetic unit uses as its first operand.

encoding.0: USE_REGISTER: the first operand is the register value read for rs1
encoding.1: USE_PC: the first operand is the address of the instruction itself

blocks.name: imm_gen
blocks.description: Combinational immediate generator. Extracts a field from the 32-bit instruction word and extends it to 32 bits, in the layout immsel selects; the meaning of each immsel code is given by its encoding table. Sign extension replicates the instruction's bit 31 into every bit above the extracted field. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: regfile
blocks.description: Register file.

blocks.name: hazard_unit
blocks.description: Combinational hazard unit. Decides when the front of the pipeline must wait and when its instructions must be thrown away. rs1_id and rs2_id are the source register numbers in the instruction in the decode stage. rd_ex, regwrite_ex and memsrc_ex are the destination register, the write enable and the write-back source of the instruction in the execute stage; is_csr_ex is 1 when that instruction is a CSR instruction, whose result is only available in the write-back stage. redirect is 1 when the execute stage has decided to take a branch or a jump. md_busy is 1 when the instruction in the execute stage is a multiply or divide whose result is not ready yet. wb_redirect is 1 when the write-back stage is taking an exception or mret. A load is an instruction whose memsrc is FROM_MEMORY. The load-use condition is 1 when the instruction in the execute stage writes a register (regwrite_ex is 1) and is a load (memsrc_ex is FROM_MEMORY) or a CSR instruction (is_csr_ex is 1), rd_ex is not zero, and rd_ex equals rs1_id or rs2_id: the value is not yet available to the instruction behind it, which must wait one cycle. The unit does not look at whether the instruction in the decode stage really reads rs1 or rs2, so it may stall once when it did not need to; it never fails to stall when it should. stall is 1 when the load-use condition is 1 or md_busy is 1: the program counter and the IF/ID register hold. md_stall equals md_busy: the ID/EX register holds. flush_if_id is 1 when redirect is 1 or wb_redirect is 1: the instruction fetched after the branch, or after the instruction that is trapping, is on the wrong path. flush_id_ex is 1 when redirect is 1, wb_redirect is 1 or the load-use condition is 1: after a redirect the instruction in the decode stage is on the wrong path, and for a load-use a bubble must go into the execute stage. flush_id_ex does not depend on md_busy, because while a multiply or divide waits the instruction in the execute stage must stay where it is. flush_ex_mem is 1 when md_busy is 1 or wb_redirect is 1: a bubble goes into the memory stage while a multiply or divide works and when an exception or mret is taken. flush_mem_wb equals wb_redirect: the instruction in the memory stage must not commit. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: id_ex
blocks.description: ID/EX pipeline register. Sits between the decode stage and the execute stage. Every output shows the value its matching input had at the last rising clock edge; nothing changes between edges, and no output depends combinationally on any input. On each rising clock edge: when rst is 1 or flush is 1, the register is cleared: is_amo_out becomes 0; amo_op_out becomes 0; irq_out becomes 0; pc_out becomes 0; pc_plus4_out becomes 0; rs1_data_out becomes 0; rs2_data_out becomes 0; imm_out becomes 0; rs1_out becomes 0; rs2_out becomes 0; rd_out becomes 0; regwrite_out becomes 0, NO_WRITE; alusrc_out becomes 0; arith_out becomes 0; opsel_out becomes 0; asel_out becomes 0; brsel_out becomes 7, NO_BRANCH; pcsel_out becomes 0, NEXT; memtype_out becomes 5, NO_ACCESS; memwrite_out becomes 0, NO_STORE; memsrc_out becomes 0; mdop_out becomes 0, MD_NONE; valid_out becomes 0, a bubble; inst_out becomes 0; xcpt_out becomes 0, no exception; cause_out becomes 0; csrop_out becomes 0, CSR_NONE; is_csr_out becomes 0; is_mret_out becomes 0; csr_imm_out becomes 0. Otherwise, when stall is 1, every output keeps its value. Otherwise every output takes the value of its matching input. A cleared register holds a bubble: it writes no register, stores nothing, takes no branch, jumps nowhere, asks for no multiply or divide and raises no exception, whatever its other outputs read. A flush is used for the instruction behind a taken branch or jump, for the bubble after a load or CSR read that the next instruction needs, and when an exception or mret is taken. A stall holds the instruction in the execute stage while a multiply or divide is still working. valid is 1 for a real instruction and 0 for a bubble; xcpt is 1 when the instruction has raised an exception that will be taken when it reaches the write-back stage, with its cause in cause; csrop, csr_imm and is_csr say what a CSR instruction does; is_mret marks mret. A cleared register holds a bubble: valid, xcpt, csrop, is_csr and is_mret are 0. irq is 1 when the exception this instruction carries is really an interrupt that was attached to it in the decode stage (xcpt is then 1 too, and cause holds the interrupt's code); a cleared register holds irq 0. is_amo is 1 for an atomic instruction and amo_op says which one (AMO_NONE for any other instruction); a cleared register holds is_amo 0 and amo_op 0.

encoding.0000: MD_NONE: not a multiply or divide instruction
encoding.0010: reserved: never produced
encoding.0011: reserved: never produced
encoding.0100: reserved: never produced
encoding.0110: reserved: never produced
encoding.0111: reserved: never produced

encoding.1001: MULH: the high 32 bits of the product, both source registers read as signed
encoding.1010: MULHSU: the high 32 bits of the product, the first source register read as signed and the second as unsigned
encoding.1011: MULHU: the high 32 bits of the product, both source registers read as unsigned

semantics.description: Why an instruction raised an exception. The value is what the machine cause register holds (zero-extended to 32 bits) when the exception is taken. encoding.0000: INSTRUCTION_ADDRESS_MISALIGNED: a taken branch or jump whose target address is not a multiple of four
encoding.0010: ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION: the instruction word is not a valid instruction, or it names a CSR that does not exist or writes one that is read-only
encoding.0011: BREAKPOINT: an ebreak instruction (irq flag 0); with the irq flag 1 it is MACHINE_SOFTWARE_INTERRUPT: the machine software interrupt is taken
encoding.0100: LOAD_ADDRESS_MISALIGNED: a load whose address is not a multiple of its size
encoding.0110: STORE_ADDRESS_MISALIGNED: a store whose address is not a multiple of its size
encoding.0111: MACHINE_TIMER_INTERRUPT: the machine timer interrupt is taken (irq flag 1 only; never produced with the irq flag 0)
encoding.1011: ECALL_FROM_M_MODE: an ecall instruction (irq flag 0); with the irq flag 1 it is MACHINE_EXTERNAL_INTERRUPT: the machine external interrupt is taken

semantics.description: What a CSR instruction does to the control and status register it names, or that the instruction is not a CSR instruction.

encoding.010: CSR_WRITE: the register becomes the source value (csrrw, csrrwi)
encoding.011: CSR_SET: the register becomes itself OR the source value (csrrs, csrrsi, source not zero)
encoding.100: CSR_CLEAR: the register becomes itself AND NOT the source value (csrrc, csrrci, source not zero)

semantics.description: Which atomic memory operation an instruction is, or that it is not an atomic instruction.

encoding.0000: AMO_NONE: not an atomic instruction
encoding.0001: AMO_LR: load-reserved: load the word and record a reservation on its address
encoding.0010: AMO_SC: store-conditional: store only if the reservation holds, and write back 0 for success or 1 for failure
encoding.0011: AMO_SWAP: write the second register's value, write back the old value
encoding.0100: AMO_ADD: write old plus the second register, write back the old value
encoding.0101: AMO_XOR: write old exclusive-or the second register, write back the old value
encoding.0110: AMO_AND: write old and the second register, write back the old value
encoding.0111: AMO_OR: write old or the second register, write back the old value
encoding.1000: AMO_MIN: write the smaller of old and the second register, both signed, write back the old value
encoding.1001: AMO_MAX: write the larger of old and the second register, both signed, write back the old value
encoding.1010: AMO_MINU: write the smaller of old and the second register, both unsigned, write back the old value
encoding.1011: AMO_MAXU: write the larger of old and the second register, both unsigned, write back the old value

blocks.name: forward_unit
blocks.description: Combinational forwarding unit. Decides, for each of the two operands of the instruction in the execute stage, whether to use the value read in the decode stage or a newer value that is still on its way to the register file. rs1 and rs2 are the source register numbers of the instruction in the execute stage. rd_mem and regwrite_mem are the destination register number and write enable of the instruction in the memory stage; rd_wb and regwrite_wb are those of the instruction in the write-back stage. fwd_a is for the first operand (rs1) and fwd_b for the second (rs2); the meaning of each code is given by its encoding table. For each operand: when regwrite_mem is 1, rd_mem is not zero and rd_mem equals the operand's register number, the code is FROM_EX_MEM; otherwise, when regwrite_wb is 1, rd_wb is not zero and rd_wb equals the operand's register number, the code is FROM_MEM_WB; otherwise the code is FROM_REGISTER. The memory stage wins over the write-back stage because it holds the newer instruction. Register zero is never forwarded, because it reads zero whatever is written to it. No clock, no reset, no state.

semantics.description: Where an execute-stage operand comes from.

encoding.00: FROM_REGISTER: the value read from the register file in the decode stage, held in the ID/EX register
encoding.01: FROM_EX_MEM: the result held in the EX/MEM register, the value the instruction now in the memory stage will write back
encoding.10: FROM_MEM_WB: the write-back value, the value the instruction now in the write-back stage is writing to the register file

semantics.description: Where an execute-stage operand comes from.

encoding.00: FROM_REGISTER: the value read from the register file in the decode stage, held in the ID/EX register
encoding.01: FROM_EX_MEM: the result held in the EX/MEM register, the value the instruction now in the memory stage will write back
encoding.10: FROM_MEM_WB: the write-back value, the value the instruction now in the write-back stage is writing to the register file

blocks.name: fwd_a_mux
blocks.description: Operand A selector: the value the execute stage uses as its first operand.

blocks.name: fwd_b_mux
blocks.description: Operand B selector: the value the execute stage uses as its second register operand and as the data a store writes.

blocks.name: alu_a_mux
blocks.description: First operand selector: the register value, or the address of the instruction itself.

blocks.name: alu_core
blocks.description: Combinational arithmetic and logic unit. The first operand is a. The second operand is b_reg when alusrc selects USE_REGISTER and b_imm when it selects USE_IMMEDIATE. y is the operation that opsel selects, applied to those two operands, with arith modifying two of the codes; the meaning of every code is given by the encoding tables for opsel, alusrc and arith. zero is 1 when every bit of y is zero and 0 otherwise. All results are 32 bits and wrap rather than saturate. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: br_comp
blocks.description: Combinational branch comparator. Compares its two 32-bit operands in the way brsel selects and drives taken to 1 when the comparison holds, 0 otherwise; the meaning of each brsel code is given by its encoding table. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: branch_adder
blocks.description: Branch target adder: the address of the instruction in the execute stage plus its immediate.

blocks.name: ex_mem
blocks.description: EX/MEM pipeline register. Sits between the execute stage and the memory stage. blocks.name: md_decode
blocks.description: Combinational decoder for the multiply and divide instructions. inst is the 32-bit instruction word. mdop says whether it is one of the eight M-extension instructions and which one; the meaning of each code is given by its encoding table. For such an instruction the top bit of mdop is 1 and its low three bits are bits 14:12 of inst (the funct3 field), so funct3 000 is MUL, 001 is MULH, 010 is MULHSU, 011 is MULHU, 100 is DIV, 101 is DIVU, 110 is REM and 111 is REMU. For every other instruction word mdop is MD_NONE. The other reserved codes are never produced. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: booth_mul
blocks.description: Iterative multiplier using radix-4 Booth's algorithm: it forms the full 64-bit product of a and b, two multiplier bits per clock cycle. a_signed says whether a is read as a signed two's complement number (1) or as an unsigned number (0); b_signed says the same for b. Let A be the value of a read that way and B the value of b read that way. The product A times B, as a 64-bit two's complement number (its low 64 bits), is delivered as hi (bits 63:32) and lo (bits 31:0) while done is 1. The unit holds these values: a state that is IDLE, RUN or DONE; a 33-bit multiplicand M; a 34-bit multiplier register Q; a 36-bit accumulator ACC; one bit QM; a step counter. On each rising clock edge, in this order: when rst is 1 the state becomes IDLE and M, Q, ACC, QM and the counter become zero. Otherwise, in IDLE: when start is 1 the unit copies its operands: M becomes the 33-bit value made of (a[31] and a_signed) followed by the 32 bits of a; Q becomes the 34-bit value made of two copies of (b[31] and b_signed) followed by the 32 bits of b; ACC becomes 0, QM becomes 0, the counter becomes 0 and the state becomes RUN; when start is 0 nothing changes. In RUN, one Booth step is made on every edge: look at the three bits Q[1], Q[0] and QM, in that order, read as a 3-bit number. T is a 36-bit value, wrapping, formed from ACC, MX (M sign-extended to 36 bits: its top bit M[32] copied into the three bits above it), and 2MX (MX shifted left one place, the top bit dropped, so a negative M gives a negative 2MX): for 000 and 111, T is ACC; for 001 and 010, T is ACC plus MX; for 011, T is ACC plus 2MX; for 100, T is ACC minus 2MX; for 101 and 110, T is ACC minus MX. Then ACC becomes T shifted right two places with its top bit kept (two copies of T[35] followed by T[35:2]), Q becomes T[1:0] followed by Q[33:2], QM becomes the old Q[1], and the counter goes up by one. When the counter was 16 before the step (this was the 17th step) the state becomes DONE. In DONE the state becomes IDLE on the next edge, whatever start is, and nothing else changes. Once a multiplication has begun it runs to the end whatever start does. done is 1 exactly when the state is DONE. While done is 1, ACC followed by Q read as one 70-bit number (ACC in the top 36 bits, Q in the low 34 bits) holds the product in its low 64 bits: lo is Q[31:0] and hi is ACC[29:0] followed by Q[33:32]. While done is 0, hi and lo are both 0. done, hi and lo depend only on the held state, not on the inputs.

blocks.name: iter_div
blocks.description: Iterative restoring divider: it divides a (the dividend) by b (the divisor) and delivers the quotient and remainder while done is 1, one quotient bit per clock cycle. is_signed says whether a and b are read as signed two's complement numbers (1) or as unsigned numbers (0). Results follow the RISC-V rules. For unsigned division the quotient is a divided by b rounded down and the remainder is a minus quotient times b. For signed division the quotient is rounded toward zero and the remainder has the sign of the dividend (or is zero). When b is 0 the quotient is all ones (FFFFFFFF) and the remainder is a, for signed and unsigned alike. When signed, a is the most negative number (80000000) and b is minus one (FFFFFFFF), the quotient is 80000000 and the remainder is 0. The unit holds: a state that is IDLE, RUN or DONE; a 33-bit remainder register R; a 32-bit quotient register Q; a 32-bit divisor register D; the original dividend A; flags neg_q, neg_r and by_zero; a step counter. On each rising clock edge, in this order: when rst is 1 the state becomes IDLE and every held value becomes zero. Otherwise, in IDLE: when start is 1 the unit copies its operands: when is_signed is 1 and a[31] is 1, Q becomes the negation of a (32 bits, wrapping), else Q becomes a; when is_signed is 1 and b[31] is 1, D becomes the negation of b, else D becomes b; R becomes 0; A becomes a; neg_q becomes 1 when is_signed is 1 and a[31] differs from b[31], else 0; neg_r becomes 1 when is_signed is 1 and a[31] is 1, else 0; by_zero becomes 1 when b is 0, else 0; the counter becomes 0; the state becomes RUN. When start is 0 nothing changes. In RUN, one step is made on every edge: S is the 33-bit value R[31:0] followed by Q[31]. When S is at least D (D taken as an unsigned number, zero-extended to 33 bits), R becomes S minus D and the new Q bit is 1; otherwise R becomes S and the new Q bit is 0. Q becomes Q[30:0] followed by the new bit, and the counter goes up by one. When the counter was 31 before the step (this was the 32nd step) the state becomes DONE. In DONE the state becomes IDLE on the next edge, whatever start is, and nothing else changes. Once a division has begun it runs to the end whatever start does. done is 1 exactly when the state is DONE. While done is 1: when by_zero is 1 the quotient is FFFFFFFF and the remainder is A; otherwise the quotient is Q, negated (32 bits, wrapping) when neg_q is 1, and the remainder is R[31:0], negated when neg_r is 1. While done is 0, quotient and remainder are both 0. done, quotient and remainder depend only on the held state, not on the inputs.

blocks.name: md_ctrl
blocks.description: Combinational control for the multiply and divide units, in the execute stage. mdop is the instruction's multiply or divide code, whose meaning is given by its encoding table. is_md is 1 when mdop is any of the eight operations (its top bit is 1). start_mul is 1 when is_md is 1 and the operation is a multiply (MUL, MULH, MULHSU or MULHU, bit 2 of mdop is 0); start_div is 1 when is_md is 1 and the operation is a divide or remainder (DIV, DIVU, REM or REMU, bit 2 of mdop is 1). For the multiplier, mul_a_signed is 1 for MUL, MULH and MULHSU and 0 for every other mdop value (including all four divides and every value that is not a multiply or divide); mul_b_signed is 1 for MUL and MULH and 0 for every other mdop value; div_signed is 1 for DIV and REM and 0 for every other mdop value. done is mul_done when start_mul is 1, div_done when start_div is 1, and 0 otherwise. busy is 1 when is_md is 1 and done is 0: the instruction is waiting for its result. md_result is the instruction's result: for MUL it is mul_lo; for MULH, MULHSU and MULHU it is mul_hi; for DIV and DIVU it is quotient; for REM and REMU it is remainder; for every other mdop it is 0. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: sys_decode
blocks.description: Combinational decoder for the instructions that are illegal, trap or touch the control and status registers. inst is the 32-bit instruction word. The word is LEGAL when bits 1:0 are 11 and it matches one of these (opcode is bits 6:0, funct3 bits 14:12, funct7 bits 31:25): LUI (opcode 0110111), AUIPC (0010111) and JAL (1101111) with any other bits; JALR (1100111) with funct3 000; a branch (1100011) with funct3 000, 001, 100, 101, 110 or 111; a load (0000011) with funct3 000, 001, 010, 100 or 101; a store (0100011) with funct3 000, 001 or 010; an immediate arithmetic instruction (0010011) with funct3 000, 010, 011, 100, 110 or 111 and any upper bits, with funct3 001 and funct7 0000000, or with funct3 101 and funct7 0000000 or 0100000; a register arithmetic instruction (0110011) with funct7 0000000 and any funct3, with funct7 0100000 and funct3 000 or 101, or with funct7 0000001 and any funct3; a fence or fence.i (opcode 0001111) with funct3 000 or 001; an atomic instruction (opcode 0101111) with funct3 010 and bits 31:27 equal to 00000, 00001, 00011, 00100, 01000, 01100, 10000, 10100, 11000 or 11100 (bits 26:25 may be anything), or with bits 31:27 equal to 00010 and bits 24:20 equal to 00000; and a system instruction (1110011) that is exactly one of four words: bits 31:0 of inst are 00000000000000000000000001110011 (hexadecimal 00000073, ecall); bits 31:0 of inst are 00000000000100000000000001110011 (hexadecimal 00100073, ebreak); bits 31:0 of inst are 00110000001000000000000001110011 (hexadecimal 30200073, mret); or bits 31:0 of inst are 00010000010100000000000001110011 (hexadecimal 10500073, wfi); or has funct3 001, 010, 011, 101, 110 or 111 (the six CSR instructions, bits 31:20 are the CSR address and bits 19:15 the source register or immediate). Every other word is illegal. xcpt is 1 and cause is ILLEGAL_INSTRUCTION for an illegal word, xcpt is 1 and cause is BREAKPOINT for ebreak, xcpt is 1 and cause is ECALL_FROM_M_MODE for ecall, and otherwise xcpt is 0 and cause is 0. is_csr is 1 for a legal CSR instruction and 0 otherwise. For a legal CSR instruction csr_imm is 1 when funct3 bit 2 is 1 (the immediate forms) and 0 otherwise, and csrop is CSR_WRITE when funct3 bits 1:0 are 01; CSR_SET when they are 10 and bits 19:15 are not zero; CSR_CLEAR when they are 11 and bits 19:15 are not zero; and CSR_READ when they are 10 or 11 and bits 19:15 are zero. For every other instruction csrop is CSR_NONE and csr_imm is 0. is_mret is 1 only for the mret word, bits 31:0 of inst are 00110000001000000000000001110011. wfi and fence change nothing. is_amo is 1 for a legal atomic instruction and 0 otherwise. amo_op, for a legal atomic instruction, is by bits 31:27: 00010 AMO_LR, 00011 AMO_SC, 00001 AMO_SWAP, 00000 AMO_ADD, 00100 AMO_XOR, 01100 AMO_AND, 01000 AMO_OR, 10000 AMO_MIN, 10100 AMO_MAX, 11000 AMO_MINU, 11100 AMO_MAXU; for every other instruction it is AMO_NONE. An atomic instruction is not an exception, not a CSR instruction and not mret. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.description: Combinational. csr_wdata is the source value of a CSR instruction: when use_imm is 1 it is rs1_field (5 bits) zero-extended to 32 bits, and otherwise it is rs1_value. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: ex_xcpt
blocks.description: Combinational exception unit for the execute stage. It adds the exceptions the execute stage can find to the one decode may already have raised, and decides the trap value. id_xcpt and id_cause are decode's exception, if any. inst and pc are the instruction and its address. memtype is the memory access type of the instruction (NO_ACCESS when it is not a load or store), memwrite is 1 for a store, alu_y is the address of the access. blocks.name: csr_file
blocks.description: Control and status register file and trap logic, in the write-back stage. It holds machine-mode state only. valid is 1 when the instruction in the write-back stage is a real one. csr_sel is the register the instruction names, by its encoding table (CSR_UNKNOWN for an address the core does not have). csrop says what a CSR instruction does (CSR_NONE for any other instruction; the reserved values 101, 110 and 111 are never produced and behave as CSR_NONE) and wdata is its source value. inst is the instruction word, used only as the trap value of an illegal CSR access. xcpt, cause, pc and tval are an exception the instruction has raised, with its address and trap value; is_mret is 1 for mret. Held state, all zero at reset: mie_bit and mpie_bit (the interrupt enable and its saved copy, bits 3 and 7 of mstatus); mtvec (bits 31:2 are held, bits 1:0 always read 0); mscratch; mepc (bits 31:1 are held, bit 0 always reads 0); mcause; mtval; mie (only bits 3, 7 and 11 are held); mcycle and minstret, each 64 bits wide, as a low and a high word. Constant registers: misa reads 40001105 hexadecimal; mvendorid, marchid, mimpid and mhartid read 0; mip reads bit 11 as ext_meip, bit 7 as ext_mtip and bit 3 as ext_msip, every other bit 0, and ignores writes (the lines are inputs, not held state); mstatus reads as mie_bit in bit 3, mpie_bit in bit 7 and bits 12:11 equal to 11, all other bits 0. cycle, instret, cycleh and instreth read the same counters as mcycle, minstret, mcycleh and minstreth (the low word of mcycle and cycle, the high word of mcycleh and cycleh, and so on) and cannot be written; neither can mvendorid, marchid, mimpid and mhartid. csr_sel names a register when it is one of the numbers 1 to 21; it names none when it is 0 or any of 22 to 31. rdata is the value of the register csr_sel names (before any write by this instruction), and 0 when csr_sel is 0 or 22 to 31. A CSR access is ILLEGAL when csrop is not CSR_NONE and either csr_sel is 0 or 22 to 31 (it names no register), or csrop is CSR_WRITE, CSR_SET or CSR_CLEAR and csr_sel is one of 14 to 21, the read-only registers (cycle, instret, cycleh, instreth, mvendorid, marchid, mimpid, mhartid). A write to any other register, misa and mip included, is not illegal: a write to misa or to mip is accepted and changes nothing. trap is 1 when valid is 1 and (xcpt is 1 or the CSR access is illegal). redirect is 1 when trap is 1, or when valid is 1, is_mret is 1 and xcpt is 0. redirect_pc is the held mtvec (bits 31:2, then 00) when trap is 1 and the held mepc otherwise. On each rising clock edge, in this order, when valid is 1: (a) when trap is 1: mepc becomes pc with bit 0 cleared; mcause becomes cause (zero-extended) when xcpt is 1, with bit 31 set as well when irq is 1 (an interrupt), and 2 when only the CSR access was illegal; mtval becomes tval when xcpt is 1 and inst when only the CSR access was illegal; mpie_bit becomes mie_bit and mie_bit becomes 0; nothing else is written and minstret does not count the instruction. (b) otherwise when is_mret is 1: mie_bit becomes mpie_bit, mpie_bit becomes 1, and minstret counts. (c) otherwise when csrop is CSR_WRITE, CSR_SET or CSR_CLEAR: the register csr_sel names becomes the new value N, which is wdata for CSR_WRITE, the old value OR wdata for CSR_SET and the old value AND NOT wdata for CSR_CLEAR; for mstatus only bits 3 and 7 are taken (into mie_bit and mpie_bit); for mtvec bits 1:0 are cleared and for mepc bit 0 is cleared; for mie only bits 3, 7 and 11 are kept; and minstret counts (unless the register written is minstret or minstreth, whose written value then stands). (d) otherwise minstret counts. minstret counts means the 64-bit minstret goes up by one. mcycle goes up by one on every edge, valid or not, unless the register written that edge is mcycle or mcycleh; reset makes every held value zero and has priority over everything. When valid is 0 nothing is written except that mcycle counts. trap, redirect, redirect_pc and rdata depend only on the inputs and the held state, not on a clock edge. irq is 1 when the exception the instruction carries (xcpt is 1) is an interrupt; it is 0 whenever xcpt is 0. Two more outputs show held state: mstatus_mie is the interrupt enable bit mie_bit, and mie_en is the three enable bits of the mie register, bit 2 being mie bit 11, bit 1 being mie bit 7 and bit 0 being mie bit 3; both depend only on the held state.

blocks.description: Combinational. pc is the address being fetched (a multiple of two). hi_addr is pc plus four (wrapping at 32 bits): the address at which the second copy of the instruction memory is read, so that it answers with the word after the one that holds pc. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.description: Combinational. pc is the address being fetched (a multiple of two). word_lo is the 32-bit word of the instruction memory that holds the address pc (the word at pc with bits 1:0 cleared) and word_hi is the word after it. inst is the 32 bits of instruction text that start at pc: when bit 1 of pc is 0 it is word_lo, and when bit 1 of pc is 1 it is word_hi bits 15:0 as the upper half and word_lo bits 31:16 as the lower half, that is {word_hi[15:0], word_lo[31:16]}. is16 is 1 when bits 1:0 of inst are not 11, which is how a 16-bit compressed instruction is told from a 32-bit one. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: rvc_q0
blocks.description: Combinational expander for the compressed instructions of one quadrant. inst is a 32-bit value of which only bits 15:2 are read: bits 1:0 are not looked at, and this block always acts as the decoder for the instructions whose bits 1:0 are 00. Write h for the 16-bit compressed instruction {inst[15:2], 2'b00}, so h[1:0] is 00 and h[k] is inst[k] for k from 2 to 15. word is the 32-bit RISC-V instruction h stands for, or, when h is reserved or not available on this core, the 16-bit value h zero-extended to 32 bits (word is then {16'b0, h}). Let f3 be h[15:13], rdp be h[4:2] + 8, rs1p be h[9:7] + 8 and rs2p be h[4:2] + 8. f3 = 000 is C.ADDI4SPN: let imm10 be the 10-bit value {h[10:7], h[12:11], h[5], h[6], 2'b00}; when imm10 is 0 the instruction is reserved, otherwise word is the I-type instruction addi rdp, x2, imm10 (the 12-bit immediate is imm10 zero-extended, opcode 0010011, funct3 000, rs1 is x2). f3 = 010 is C.LW: let imm7 be the 7-bit value {h[5], h[12:10], h[6], 2'b00}; word is the I-type lw rdp, imm7(rs1p) (immediate imm7 zero-extended to 12 bits, opcode 0000011, funct3 010). f3 = 110 is C.SW: with the same imm7, word is the S-type sw rs2p, imm7(rs1p) (immediate imm7 zero-extended to 12 bits, opcode 0100011, funct3 010). Every other value of f3 (001, 011, 100, 101, 111) is reserved or needs a floating-point extension this core does not have. Registers written x0 to x31 are 5-bit numbers; a compact register number from a 3-bit field c is c + 8. No clock, no reset, no state.

Write h for the 16-bit compressed instruction {inst[15:2], 2'b01}, so h[1:0] is 01 and h[k] is inst[k] for k from 2 to 15. word is the 32-bit RISC-V instruction h stands for, or, when h is reserved or not available on this core, the 16-bit value h zero-extended to 32 bits (word is then {16'b0, h}). Let f3 be h[15:13] and rd be h[11:7]. Let imm6 be the 6-bit value {h[12], h[6:2]} and simm be imm6 sign-extended to 12 bits. f3 = 000 is C.ADDI (and C.NOP): word is the I-type addi rd, rd, simm (opcode 0010011, funct3 000). f3 = 010 is C.LI: word is the I-type addi rd, x0, simm. f3 = 001 is C.JAL and f3 = 101 is C.J: let off12 be the 12-bit value {h[12], h[8], h[10:9], h[6], h[7], h[2], h[11], h[5:3], 1'b0} and joff be off12 sign-extended to 21 bits; word is the J-type jal with immediate joff (opcode 1101111) and rd x1 for C.JAL, x0 for C.J. f3 = 011: when rd is 2 this is C.ADDI16SP: let imm10 be the 10-bit value {h[12], h[4:3], h[5], h[2], h[6], 4'b0000}; when imm10 is 0 the instruction is reserved, otherwise word is the I-type addi x2, x2, imm10 sign-extended to 12 bits; when rd is not 2 this is C.LUI: when imm6 is 0 the instruction is reserved, otherwise word is the U-type lui rd with the 20-bit immediate imm6 sign-extended to 20 bits (opcode 0110111). f3 = 100 is the group of arithmetic instructions on compact registers: let rdq be h[9:7] + 8, rs2q be h[4:2] + 8 and shamt be h[6:2]. When h[11:10] is 00 (C.SRLI): reserved if h[12] is 1, otherwise word is the I-type srli rdq, rdq, shamt, whose immediate field is {7'b0000000, shamt} (opcode 0010011, funct3 101). When h[11:10] is 01 (C.SRAI): reserved if h[12] is 1, otherwise the I-type srai rdq, rdq, shamt whose immediate field is {7'b0100000, shamt} (opcode 0010011, funct3 101). When h[11:10] is 10 (C.ANDI): word is the I-type andi rdq, rdq, simm (opcode 0010011, funct3 111). When h[11:10] is 11: reserved if h[12] is 1; otherwise the R-type instruction (opcode 0110011, rs1 and rd both rdq, rs2 rs2q) chosen by h[6:5]: 00 sub (funct7 0100000, funct3 000), 01 xor (funct7 0000000, funct3 100), 10 or (funct7 0000000, funct3 110), 11 and (funct7 0000000, funct3 111). f3 = 110 is C.BEQZ and f3 = 111 is C.BNEZ: let off9 be the 9-bit value {h[12], h[6:5], h[2], h[11:10], h[4:3], 1'b0} and boff be off9 sign-extended to 13 bits; let rs1q be h[9:7] + 8; word is the B-type branch with immediate boff, rs1 rs1q, rs2 x0 and opcode 1100011, with funct3 000 (beq) for C.BEQZ and 001 (bne) for C.BNEZ. Registers written x0 to x31 are 5-bit numbers; a compact register number from a 3-bit field c is c + 8. Instruction layouts: I-type is {imm[11:0], rs1, funct3, rd, opcode}; S-type is {imm[11:5], rs2, rs1, funct3, imm[4:0], opcode}; B-type is {imm[12], imm[10:5], rs2, rs1, funct3, imm[4:1], imm[11], opcode}; U-type is {imm[31:12], rd, opcode}; J-type is {imm[20], imm[10:1], imm[11], imm[19:12], rd, opcode}; R-type is {funct7, rs2, rs1, funct3, rd, opcode}. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: rvc_q2
blocks.description: Combinational expander for the compressed instructions of one quadrant. inst is a 32-bit value of which only bits 15:2 are read: bits 1:0 are not looked at, and this block always acts as the decoder for the instructions whose bits 1:0 are 10. Write h for the 16-bit compressed instruction {inst[15:2], 2'b10}, so h[1:0] is 10 and h[k] is inst[k] for k from 2 to 15. word is the 32-bit RISC-V instruction h stands for, or, when h is reserved or not available on this core, the 16-bit value h zero-extended to 32 bits (word is then {16'b0, h}). Let f3 be h[15:13], rd be h[11:7] and rs2 be h[6:2]. f3 = 000 is C.SLLI: reserved if h[12] is 1, otherwise word is the I-type slli rd, rd, shamt with shamt h[6:2], whose immediate field is {7'b0000000, h[6:2]} (opcode 0010011, funct3 001). f3 = 010 is C.LWSP: reserved when rd is 0; otherwise let off8 be the 8-bit value {h[3:2], h[12], h[6:4], 2'b00} and word be the I-type lw rd, off8(x2) (immediate off8 zero-extended to 12 bits, rs1 x2, opcode 0000011, funct3 010). f3 = 100: when h[12] is 0 and rs2 is 0 this is C.JR: reserved when rd is 0, otherwise word is the I-type jalr x0, 0(rd) (opcode 1100111, funct3 000, immediate 0, rd field x0, rs1 rd); when h[12] is 0 and rs2 is not 0 this is C.MV: word is the R-type add rd, x0, rs2 (funct7 0000000, funct3 000, opcode 0110011); when h[12] is 1 and rs2 is 0 and rd is 0 this is C.EBREAK: word is 32'h00100073; when h[12] is 1 and rs2 is 0 and rd is not 0 this is C.JALR: word is the I-type jalr x1, 0(rd) (opcode 1100111, funct3 000, immediate 0, rd field x1, rs1 rd); when h[12] is 1 and rs2 is not 0 this is C.ADD: word is the R-type add rd, rd, rs2 (funct7 0000000, funct3 000, opcode 0110011). f3 = 110 is C.SWSP: let off8 be the 8-bit value {h[8:7], h[12:9], 2'b00}; word is the S-type sw rs2, off8(x2) (immediate off8 zero-extended to 12 bits, rs1 x2, funct3 010, opcode 0100011). Every other value of f3 (001, 011, 101, 111) is reserved or needs a floating-point extension this core does not have. Registers written x0 to x31 are 5-bit numbers; a compact register number from a 3-bit field c is c + 8. Instruction layouts: I-type is {imm[11:0], rs1, funct3, rd, opcode}; S-type is {imm[11:5], rs2, rs1, funct3, imm[4:0], opcode}; B-type is {imm[12], imm[10:5], rs2, rs1, funct3, imm[4:1], imm[11], opcode}; U-type is {imm[31:12], rd, opcode}; J-type is {imm[20], imm[10:1], imm[11], imm[19:12], rd, opcode}; R-type is {funct7, rs2, rs1, funct3, rd, opcode}. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: rvc_select
blocks.description: Combinational. inst is the 32 bits of instruction text from the fetch aligner, and q0, q1 and q2 are the expanded forms of its low half in each compressed quadrant. inst_out is inst when bits 1:0 of inst are 11 (a 32-bit instruction), q0 when they are 00, q1 when they are 01 and q2 when they are 10. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: region_decode
blocks.description: Combinational address decoder for the data side, in the memory stage. addr is the 32-bit address of an access. There are five regions that do not overlap, and every other address belongs to none. The RAM is the 16 MB from 80000000 to 80FFFFFF hexadecimal: bits 31:24 of addr are 10000000. The CLINT is the 64 KB from 02000000 to 0200FFFF: bits 31:16 of addr are 0000001000000000. The PLIC is the 64 MB from 0C000000 to 0FFFFFFF: bits 31:26 of addr are 000011. The UART is the 4 KB from 10000000 to 10000FFF: bits 31:12 of addr are 00010000000000000000. The GPU is the 16 MB from 30000000 to 30FFFFFF: bits 31:24 of addr are 00110000. For instance the first 4 KB of the RAM are the addresses whose bits 31:12 of addr are 10000000000000000000, and the first 4 KB of the GPU those whose bits 31:12 of addr are 00110000000000000000. sel_ram, sel_clint, sel_plic, sel_uart and sel_gpu are 1 for the region addr is in and 0 otherwise; is_io is 1 when addr is in the CLINT, PLIC, UART or GPU region. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: bus_ctl
blocks.description: Combinational. The write and read strobes of the data-side regions, in the memory stage. sel_ram, sel_clint, sel_plic, sel_uart and sel_gpu say which region the access is in (at most one is 1). memwrite is 1 for a store that is really going to happen (it has already been cancelled for an exception or a trap). ram_we, clint_we, plic_we, uart_we and gpu_we are memwrite and the matching select: 1 when memwrite is 1 and that select is 1, 0 otherwise. memsrc is the write-back source of the instruction in the memory stage: a load is memsrc 01 (FROM_MEMORY). valid is 1 when the instruction in the memory stage is a real one, xcpt is 1 when it has raised an exception and kill is 1 when an older instruction is trapping in write-back this cycle. A device read happens, and so can have a side effect, only when memsrc is 01, valid is 1, xcpt is 0 and kill is 0: plic_re, uart_re and gpu_re are 1 when that holds and sel_plic, sel_uart or sel_gpu respectively is 1, and 0 otherwise. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: clint_decode
blocks.description: Combinational. Names the CLINT register an address picks. addr is the 32-bit address of an access to the CLINT region; only bits 15:2 of addr are used (the word), so bits 31:16 and 1:0 do not matter. idx is a 3-bit number: 1 (msip) when bits 15:2 of addr are 00000000000000; 2 (mtimecmp, low word, offset 4000 hexadecimal) when bits 15:2 of addr are 01000000000000; 3 (mtimecmp, high word, offset 4004) when bits 15:2 of addr are 01000000000001; 4 (mtime, low word, offset BFF8) when bits 15:2 of addr are 10111111111110; 5 (mtime, high word, offset BFFC) when bits 15:2 of addr are 10111111111111; and 0 (no register) for every other value of those bits. idx is never 6 or 7. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: plic_decode
blocks.description: Combinational. Names the PLIC register an address picks. addr is the 32-bit address of an access to the PLIC region; only bits 21:2 of addr are used (the word), so bits 31:22 and 1:0 do not matter. idx is a 6-bit number: for n from 1 to 31, idx is n (the priority register of source n, offset 4 times n) when the word is n, that is when bits 21:2 of addr are the 20-bit binary number n; for instance bits 21:2 of addr are 00000000000000000001 for source 1, 00000000000000001010 for source 10 and 00000000000000011111 for source 31. idx is 32 (pending, offset 1000 hexadecimal) when bits 21:2 of addr are 00000000010000000000; 33 (enable, offset 2000) when bits 21:2 of addr are 00000000100000000000; 34 (threshold, offset 200000) when bits 21:2 of addr are 10000000000000000000; 35 (claim/complete, offset 200004) when bits 21:2 of addr are 10000000000000000001; 0 (source 0, which has no register) when bits 21:2 of addr are 00000000000000000000; and 63 (no register) for every other word. idx is never 36 to 62. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: io_mux
blocks.description: Combinational. y is clint_rdata when sel_clint is 1, plic_rdata when sel_plic is 1, uart_rdata when sel_uart is 1, gpu_rdata when sel_gpu is 1, and 0 when none of the four is 1. At most one select is 1 at a time. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: io_load
blocks.description: Combinational. raw is what a device register returned, already in its low bits. memtype is the access type of the load, with the meaning its encoding table gives. rdata is: for MEM_BYTE, raw bits 7:0 sign-extended to 32 bits; for MEM_BYTE_U, raw bits 7:0 zero-extended; for MEM_HALF, raw bits 15:0 sign-extended; for MEM_HALF_U, raw bits 15:0 zero-extended; for every other code (MEM_WORD, NO_ACCESS and the reserved codes) raw unchanged. The low address bits are not used: a device returns the register's value in the low bits whichever byte of the word was addressed. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: load_sel
blocks.description: Load value selector: the data memory's value, or a device's.

blocks.name: clint
blocks.description: Core-local interruptor, the register layout of QEMU's virt machine (one hart). idx, a 3-bit number, names the register an access picks: 1 is msip (bit 0 only; the other bits read 0 and ignore writes); 2 and 3 are the low and high words of mtimecmp (64 bits); 4 and 5 are the low and high words of mtime (64 bits); 0, 6 and 7 name no register, which reads 0 and ignores writes. we is 1 for a store to this region, with wdata the word stored. rdata is the register idx names (before this cycle's write) and 0 when it names none; it depends only on idx and the held state. At reset msip is 0, mtime is 0 and mtimecmp is all ones, so no timer interrupt is pending until software sets mtimecmp. On each rising clock edge, after reset: when we is 1 the register idx names is written (msip from wdata bit 0, a half of mtimecmp or of mtime from wdata); and mtime goes up by one (wrapping at 64 bits), except that on an edge with a store to either half of mtime that half becomes wdata and the other half keeps its value (mtime does not count on that edge). msip is the held msip bit. mtip is 1 when the 64-bit unsigned value of mtime is greater than or equal to the 64-bit value of mtimecmp, as held (before this edge), and 0 otherwise.

blocks.name: plic_regs
blocks.description: The held configuration of a platform-level interrupt controller with one source, source 10. idx is a 6-bit number naming the register of an access, we is 1 for a store, and wdata is the word stored. Held state, all 0 at reset: prio (3 bits), en (1 bit) and thr (3 bits). At a clock edge on which we is 1: when idx is 10, prio takes wdata bits 2:0; when idx is 33, en takes wdata bit 10; when idx is 34, thr takes wdata bits 2:0; for every other idx nothing changes. At a clock edge on which we is 0 nothing changes. The outputs prio, en and thr are the held values, from the held state only.

blocks.name: plic_gateway
blocks.description: The interrupt gateway of a platform-level interrupt controller with one source. irq10 is the level input of the source; claim and complete are one-cycle strobes. Held state, both 0 at reset: pending and in_service. At each clock edge, in this order, using the values held before the edge for the tests: first, pending becomes 1 when irq10 is 1 and neither pending nor in_service is 1; second, when complete is 1, in_service becomes 0 and pending becomes 1 if irq10 is 1; third, when claim is 1, pending becomes 0 and in_service becomes 1. The output pending is the held pending flag, from the held state only.

blocks.name: plic_logic
blocks.description: Combinational. The read side and the strobes of a platform-level interrupt controller with one source, source 10. idx names the register of an access; we is 1 for a store and re is 1 for a load that will really happen; wdata is the word stored; pending, prio (3 bits), en and thr (3 bits) are the held state of the source. cand is 1 when pending is 1, en is 1 and prio is greater than thr (as unsigned numbers), and 0 otherwise. meip is cand. rdata, a 32-bit word, is: prio zero-extended when bits 5:0 of idx are 001010; 1024 when pending is 1 and 0 when it is 0 if bits 5:0 of idx are 100000; 1024 when en is 1 and 0 when it is 0 if bits 5:0 of idx are 100001; thr zero-extended when bits 5:0 of idx are 100010; 10 when cand is 1 and 0 when it is 0 if bits 5:0 of idx are 100011; and 0 for every other idx. claim is 1 when re is 1, idx is 35 and cand is 1, and 0 otherwise. complete is 1 when we is 1, idx is 35 and bits 4:0 of wdata are 01010, and 0 otherwise. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: uart16550
blocks.description: A 16550-style UART with a byte interface, the register layout NuttX's 16550 driver and QEMU's virt machine use, one byte per register. addr is the 32-bit address of an access; bits 2:0 pick the register. we is 1 for a store, with wdata bits 7:0 the byte stored; re is 1 for a load that will really happen. Held state, all 0 at reset: the interrupt enable register IER (4 bits), the line control register LCR (8 bits; its bit 7 is the divisor latch access bit, DLAB), the modem control register MCR (5 bits), the scratch register SCR (8 bits), the divisor latch low byte DLL and high byte DLM (8 bits each), the FIFO-enabled flag FE, the receive buffer RBR (8 bits) with its data-ready flag DR, and the transmit-empty interrupt flag TXF. Reads: rdata has the byte in bits 7:0 and 0 in bits 31:8, and depends only on addr and the held state. Offset 0 reads DLL when DLAB is 1 and RBR when DLAB is 0. Offset 1 reads DLM when DLAB is 1 and IER (bits 7:4 are 0) when DLAB is 0. Offset 2 reads the interrupt identification register: bit 0 is 0 when an interrupt is pending and 1 when none is; bits 3:1 are 010 when the receive interrupt is pending, otherwise 001 when the transmit interrupt is pending, otherwise 000; bits 5:4 are 0; bits 7:6 are 11 when FE is 1 and 00 otherwise. Offset 3 reads LCR. Offset 4 reads MCR (bits 7:5 are 0). Offset 5 reads the line status register: bit 0 is DR, bits 5 and 6 are 1 (the transmitter is always empty), every other bit is 0. Offset 6 reads 0 (the modem status register). Offset 7 reads SCR. The receive interrupt is pending when IER bit 0 is 1 and DR is 1. The transmit interrupt is pending when IER bit 1 is 1 and TXF is 1. irq is 1 when the receive interrupt or the transmit interrupt is pending. tx_valid is 1 and tx_data is wdata bits 7:0 in a cycle when we is 1, addr bits 2:0 are 0 and DLAB is 0 (a byte to transmit); otherwise tx_valid is 0 and tx_data is 0; they depend only on the inputs and the held state. On each rising clock edge, when rst is 1 everything held becomes 0; otherwise these happen in this order, a later one overriding an earlier one for the same state. (1) Reads: when re is 1 and addr bits 2:0 are 0 and DLAB is 0, DR becomes 0; when re is 1 and addr bits 2:0 are 2 and the interrupt identification register (as read this cycle) has bits 3:1 equal to 001, TXF becomes 0. (2) Stores, by addr bits 2:0 when we is 1: offset 0 with DLAB 1 writes DLL; offset 0 with DLAB 0 transmits the byte and sets TXF to 1; offset 1 with DLAB 1 writes DLM; offset 1 with DLAB 0 writes IER (low 4 bits) and, when that write takes IER bit 1 from 0 to 1, sets TXF to 1; offset 2 sets FE to wdata bit 0 and, when wdata bit 1 is 1, sets DR to 0; offset 3 writes LCR; offset 4 writes MCR (low 5 bits); offset 7 writes SCR; stores to offsets 5 and 6 change nothing. (3) Receive: when rx_valid is 1 the byte rx_data replaces RBR and DR becomes 1.

blocks.name: amo_ctl
blocks.description: Combinational. is_amo is 1 for an atomic instruction. The other inputs are what the ordinary decoder drives; each output is that input, except that when is_amo is 1 the outputs are: immsel_out NO_IMMEDIATE (101), alusrc_out USE_IMMEDIATE (1), arith_out LOGICAL (0), opsel_out ADD_SUB (000), asel_out USE_REGISTER (0), memtype_out MEM_WORD (010), memsrc_out FROM_MEMORY (01) and memwrite_out NO_STORE (0). That makes the arithmetic unit compute rs1 plus zero, the address of the atomic access. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: amo_active
blocks.description: Combinational. active is 1 when the instruction in the memory stage performs its atomic access: valid is 1 and is_amo is 1 and sel_ram is 1 and xcpt is 0 and kill is 0, and 0 otherwise. valid is 1 when the instruction is a real one, is_amo is 1 when it is an atomic instruction, sel_ram is 1 when its address is in RAM, xcpt is 1 when it has raised an exception and kill is 1 when an older instruction is trapping in write-back. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: amo_core
blocks.description: Combinational. Atomic memory operations in the memory stage. active is 1 when the instruction performs its atomic access, is_amo is 1 when it is an atomic instruction and amo_op says which (the meaning is given by its encoding table). rs2 is the value of the instruction's second register. old is the 32-bit word the data memory reads at the address of the access. kill is 1 when an older instruction is trapping in write-back. match is 1 when the reservation held for the address of this access matches it. Outputs: use_sc is 1 when is_amo is 1 and amo_op is AMO_SC, and 0 otherwise; sc_result is 0 when match is 1 and 1 otherwise (as a 32-bit value); we is 1 when active is 1 and either amo_op is one of AMO_SWAP, AMO_ADD, AMO_XOR, AMO_AND, AMO_OR, AMO_MIN, AMO_MAX, AMO_MINU, AMO_MAXU, or amo_op is AMO_SC and match is 1, and 0 otherwise; wdata is the new word: for AMO_SWAP rs2, AMO_ADD old plus rs2 (wrapping at 32 bits), AMO_XOR old xor rs2, AMO_AND old and rs2, AMO_OR old or rs2, AMO_MIN the smaller of old and rs2 read as signed 32-bit values, AMO_MAX the larger, AMO_MINU the smaller read as unsigned, AMO_MAXU the larger read as unsigned, and for every other amo_op (AMO_SC, AMO_LR, AMO_NONE, the reserved codes) rs2; set_rsv is 1 when active is 1 and amo_op is AMO_LR, and 0 otherwise; clr_rsv is 1 when kill is 1, or when active is 1 and amo_op is AMO_SC, and 0 otherwise. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: amo_rsv
blocks.description: The reservation of load-reserved and store-conditional. set and clear are one-cycle strobes and addr is the 32-bit address of the access. Held state, all 0 at reset: rsv_valid (1 bit) and rsv_word (30 bits, the word address, addr bits 31:2, at the last set). On each rising clock edge: when rst is 1, rsv_valid and rsv_word become 0; otherwise when clear is 1, rsv_valid becomes 0 and rsv_word is unchanged; otherwise when set is 1, rsv_valid becomes 1 and rsv_word becomes addr bits 31:2. The outputs, from the held state only: rsv_valid is the held flag, and rsv_addr is a 32-bit value with rsv_word in bits 31:2 and 0 in bits 1:0.

blocks.name: amo_match
blocks.description: Combinational. match is 1 when rsv_valid is 1 and bits 31:2 of addr equal bits 31:2 of rsv_addr, and 0 otherwise (bits 1:0 of both are not looked at). No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: sc_sel

blocks.name: ram_we_merge

blocks.name: dmem1

blocks.name: dmem2
blocks.description: Data memory: the RAM. Only the low 22 address bits pick the byte (the bus decides whether the access is to RAM at all). The meaning of each memtype and memwrite code is given by their encoding tables.

blocks.name: dmem3
blocks.description: Data memory: the RAM. Only the low 22 address bits pick the byte (the bus decides whether the access is to RAM at all). The meaning of each memtype and memwrite code is given by their encoding tables.

blocks.name: ram_bank_we
blocks.description: Combinational. The RAM is four banks of 4 MB each, numbered 0 to 3; the bank an address is in is bits 23:22 of addr (00 is bank 0, 01 is bank 1, 10 is bank 2, 11 is bank 3). we0, we1, we2 and we3 are 1 when we is 1 and addr is in bank 0, 1, 2 or 3 respectively, and 0 otherwise, so at most one of them is 1. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: ram_rdata_mux
blocks.description: Combinational. The RAM is four banks, and the bank an address is in is bits 23:22 of addr. y is rdata0 when those bits are 00, rdata1 when they are 01, rdata2 when they are 10 and rdata3 when they are 11. No clock, no reset, no state.

blocks.name: gpu_bridge
blocks.description: Bridge from the SoC's memory stage to the GPU's host bus. Inputs: gpu_we (a store to the GPU window that is really happening), gpu_re (a load from it that is really happening), addr (32 bits, the access address), wdata (32, the store data), memtype (3, the access type: 2 is a word; 6 and 7 are reserved codes that act as a word; every other code is narrower or no access), host_rdata (32) and host_rvalid from the host bus. Outputs: host_en, host_we, host_addr (32), host_wdata (32) to the host bus, and rdata (32), what a load from the window returns. Translation, with off = addr bits 23:0: off from 000000 to 00FFFF hexadecimal is mapped to host address 30000000 | off bits 15:0 (control registers); 010000 to 0107FF to off bits 10:0, zero-extended (instruction memory); 020000 to 021FFF to 10000000 | off bits 12:0 (global memory); 030000 to 030FFF to 20000000 | off bits 11:0 (shared memory); 100000 to 1257FF to 40000000 | off bits 17:0 (video memory); 140000 to 1657FF to 40040000 | off bits 17:0 (depth memory); 180000 to 1807FF to 50000000 | off bits 10:0 (texture). Every other off is unmapped. host_addr is the mapped host address, 0 when unmapped. Outputs, at once: word = (memtype is 2, 6 or 7); host_we = mapped & gpu_we & word; host_en = host_we | (mapped & gpu_re); host_wdata = wdata; rdata = host_rdata when host_rvalid is 1, otherwise the register rdata_r. So a narrower store, or any access to an unmapped offset, is dropped. One register, rdata_r (32 bits): on each rising edge it becomes 0 when rst is 1, else takes host_rdata when host_rvalid is 1, else keeps its value. The host bus answers a read one cycle after the request (host_rvalid = 1 then), so a load returns the result of the previous GPU read and starts its own: a driver reads a GPU address twice and keeps the second value, and two loads in consecutive cycles work because the second sees host_rdata directly.

blocks.name: g_warp_sched
blocks.description: Warp scheduler, round robin. A warp is ready when it is active, has no instruction in flight and is not waiting at a barrier: ready = active & ~inflight & ~waiting (bit w for warp w). When enable is 1 and some warp is ready, fire = 1 and fwid is the first ready warp in the order ptr+1, ptr+2, ptr+3, ptr+4 (modulo 4), where ptr is a 2-bit register holding the warp chosen last; otherwise fire = 0 and fwid = 0. fire and fwid follow the inputs and ptr at once (combinationally). On each rising edge: when rst or start is 1, ptr becomes 3 (so warp 0 is chosen first); otherwise when fire is 1, ptr becomes fwid; otherwise ptr keeps its value.

blocks.name: g_warp_table
blocks.description: Per-warp state for 4 warps: a 32-bit pc, a 4-bit thread mask and an in-flight bit each. A warp is active when its mask is not 0. Outputs, combinational from the state and fwid: sel_pc and sel_tmask are warp fwid's pc and mask; active and inflight have one bit per warp (bit w for warp w); busy is 1 when any warp is active or in flight. On each rising edge, the first of these that applies: (1) rst is 1: every pc, mask and in-flight bit becomes 0. (2) start is 1: warp 0 gets pc = start_pc, mask 0001; warps 1 to 3 get pc 0 and mask 0000; every in-flight bit becomes 0. (3) otherwise three independent events apply, all computed from the values before this edge (a later event overrides an earlier one only on the field it names): - commit (when commit is 1): warp cwid gets pc = c_pc, mask = c_tmask and in-flight = 0. - fire (when fire is 1): warp fwid's in-flight bit becomes 1. It does not depend on spawn_mask and does not stop a spawn. - spawn: each warp w with spawn_mask bit w = 1 whose mask was 0000 and whose in-flight bit was 0 before this edge gets pc = spawn_pc and mask = 0001 (its in-flight bit is not touched by spawn). A spawn's pc and mask override a commit's on the same warp; this cannot happen in operation, but the block defines it.

blocks.name: g_pipe_ctrl
blocks.description:
Pipeline control, combinational. The X stage is busy while it holds a division whose result is not ready, a memory access
    the load-store unit has not finished, or while the graphics units ask for another cycle (g_busy, the texture unit's
    one-cycle read): x_busy = (dx_valid & ((unit is DIV & div_ready is 0) | (unit is LSU & lsu_ready is 0))) | g_busy, with unit
    read through its encoding table. stall = x_busy (the S, D and X stages hold their instructions). advance = dx_valid &
    !x_busy: the instruction in X completes at the next rising edge. sched_en = running & !x_busy. fetch_idx = bits 10:2 of sf_pc
    when x_busy is 1, otherwise bits 10:2 of sel_pc: the instruction-memory word to read, so that a held D stage keeps seeing its
    own instruction.

blocks.name: g_sf_reg

On each rising edge: when rst is 1 or clear is 1 every field becomes 0 (so valid_out becomes 0: a bubble); otherwise when hold is 1 every field keeps its value; otherwise every field takes its input. The fields: valid (1 bits), wid (2 bits), pc (32 bits), tmask (4 bits).

blocks.name: g_decode
blocks.description: Instruction decoder, combinational, for RV32IM with CSR reads and the GPU's SIMT (custom-0, opcode 0x0B) and tensor (custom-1, opcode 0x2B) instructions. Fields copied from inst every time: rs1 = bits 19:15, rs2 = bits 24:20, rd = bits 11:7, csr_addr = bits 31:20, br_op = mem_size = simt_op = funct3 (bits 14:12), md_op = funct3 bits 1:0, tensor_op = funct3 bits 1:0, gfx_op = funct3 (bits 14:12), simt_mode = instruction bits 26:25 (the two lowest bits of funct7). Every other output has a default unless the instruction's class below sets it: unit NONE, alu_op ADD, a_sel 0, b_sel 0, immsel NO_IMMEDIATE, wb_src ALU, regwrite 0, ctrl NONE, mem_store 0, illegal 0, gfx 0. The classes (op = bits 6:0, f3 = funct3, f7 = funct7): LUI (0x37): unit ALU, alu_op PASS_B, b_sel 1, immsel IMM_U, regwrite 1. AUIPC (0x17): unit ALU, alu_op ADD, a_sel 1, b_sel 1, immsel IMM_U, regwrite 1. JAL (0x6F): unit ALU, a_sel 1, b_sel 1, immsel IMM_J, wb_src LINK, regwrite 1, ctrl JAL. JALR (0x67 with f3 0): unit ALU, b_sel 1, immsel IMM_I, wb_src LINK, regwrite 1, ctrl JALR. Branch (0x63, f3 not 2 or 3): unit ALU, immsel IMM_B, ctrl BRANCH. Load (0x03, f3 0, 1, 2, 4 or 5): unit LSU, b_sel 1, immsel IMM_I, wb_src LOAD, regwrite 1. Store (0x23, f3 0, 1 or 2): unit LSU, b_sel 1, immsel IMM_S, mem_store 1. OP-IMM (0x13): b_sel 1, immsel IMM_I, regwrite 1, unit ALU, alu_op by f3: 0 ADD, 2 SLT, 3 SLTU, 4 XOR, 6 OR, 7 AND, 1 SLL (only with f7 0), 5 SRL (f7 0) or SRA (f7 0x20); any other f3/f7 is illegal. OP (0x33): regwrite 1; f7 0: unit ALU, alu_op by f3: 0 ADD, 1 SLL, 2 SLT, 3 SLTU, 4 XOR, 5 SRL, 6 OR, 7 AND; f7 0x20 with f3 0: SUB, with f3 5: SRA (unit ALU); f7 0x20 with any f3 other than 0 and 5 (that is 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7) is illegal, as is any f7 other than 0, 0x20 and 1; f7 1: unit MUL with wb_src MUL when f3 < 4, unit DIV with wb_src DIV otherwise; anything else is illegal. FENCE (0x0F, any f3): the defaults (nothing happens). SYSTEM (0x73): f3 2, 3, 6 or 7 with rs1 = 0 is a CSR read: unit CSR, wb_src CSR, regwrite 1; anything else (a CSR write, ecall, ebreak, mret) is illegal. SIMT (0x0B): legal when f3 <= 4 with f7 = 0, or f3 = 5 with f7 <= 2, or f3 = 6 with f7 <= 3: unit SIMT, wb_src SIMT, regwrite 1 for f3 5 and 6 (vote, shuffle), else 0; otherwise illegal. Tensor (0x2B with f7 0 and f3 <= 3): legal when f3 0 has rd = 0, f3 1 always, f3 2 has rd = 0, f3 3 has rd, rs1 and rs2 all 0: unit TENSOR, wb_src TENSOR, regwrite 1 for f3 1, else 0; otherwise illegal. Graphics (opcode 0x5B = 7'b1011011, custom-2), only with f7 = 0: f3 0 (gfx.cfg) or 5 (pix) is legal when rd = 0, with gfx = 1 and every other output its default (so unit is NONE and regwrite 0); f3 1 (rast), 3 (rast.edge), 4 (tex) or 6 (ztest) is legal with any rd, rs1 and rs2, with gfx = 1, regwrite = 1 and every other output its default (unit NONE, wb_src ALU); f3 2 or 7, or f7 not 0, is illegal. Any other instruction is illegal. An illegal instruction has every default except illegal = 1.

In IDLE with start: take a, b and md_op, count = 0, go to BUSY. In BUSY: when count is 31 go to DONE, otherwise count + 1 (BUSY lasts exactly 32 cycles, one quotient bit per cycle). Note that when tmask is 4'b0000 sel0 is 1 and the others are 0, so fa and fb are lane 0 (not lane 3, not 0): the same lane 0 that is used when lane 0 is active. p4 = pc + 4. When valid is 0 or unit is not SIMT: c_pc = br_next_pc, c_tmask = tmask and every other output is 0. Otherwise c_pc = p4 and c_tmask = tmask unless set below, and by simt_op: TMC: c_tmask = fa bits 3:0; clear = 1 when that is 0 (the warp ends and its stack empties). WSPAWN: spawn_mask bit w (w = 1, 2, 3) = 1 when w < fa (unsigned), bit 0 = 0; spawn_pc = fb. SPLIT: pred = the active lanes whose a lane is not 0, T = tmask & pred, F = tmask & ~pred. When depth + n > 8 (depth is a 4-bit input that never exceeds 8 in operation, but the sum is compared without wrapping), where n is 2 when both T and F are non-empty and 1 otherwise: err = 1 and nothing is pushed. Otherwise push = n with e0 = (mask tmask, pc 0, fall 1). When n is 2 (both T and F non-empty): e1 = (mask F, pc p4, fall 0) and c_tmask = T. When n is 1 (every active lane agrees, so T or F is empty): there is no e1 and c_tmask = tmask, unchanged, even if the predicate is false in every lane (T is then empty, but the mask does not become 0). JOIN: when depth is 0, err = 1; otherwise pop = 1, c_tmask = top_mask, and c_pc = p4 when top_fall is 1, else top_pc. BAR: bar_arrive = 1, bar_id = fa bits 1:0, bar_count = fb when fb < 7, else 7; err = 1 when fa > 3. VOTE, SHFL and the code 111: nothing more. push, pop, clear, spawn_mask and bar_arrive are forced to 0 whenever advance is 0, so they act only at the edge where the instruction completes. Only those five depend on advance. All the other outputs (c_pc, c_tmask, e0_*, e1_*, spawn_pc, bar_id, bar_count, err) are computed as above whatever advance is, including when advance is 0: for example a BAR with fa > 3 has err = 1 and bar_count set, and a WSPAWN has spawn_pc = fb, even when advance is 0. Every unset field of e0 and e1 is 0.

blocks.name: g_ipdom
blocks.description: Divergence stacks: one stack of up to 8 entries for each of the 4 warps; an entry is a 4-bit mask, a 32-bit pc and a fall bit. Outputs, combinational from the state and wid: depth (0 to 8) of warp wid's stack, and its top entry (the one pushed last) as top_mask, top_pc and top_fall, all 0 when the stack is empty. On each rising edge: when rst or clear_all is 1, every stack becomes empty. Otherwise, when en is 1, on warp wid's stack, the first of these that applies: clear empties it; pop removes the top entry (nothing when empty); push 1 adds e0; push 2 adds e0 and then e1 (so e1 is on top). A push that would take the stack past 8 entries changes nothing.

blocks.name: g_barrier_unit
blocks.description: Barriers: four barriers, each with a 4-bit arrived mask (bit w: warp w has arrived), and a 4-bit waiting register (bit w: warp w waits), which is the output. On each rising edge: when rst or clear_all is 1, every arrived mask and waiting bit becomes 0. Otherwise when en is 1: let m = arrived[bar_id] | (1 << wid). When the number of 1 bits in m is at least bar_count, the barrier releases: arrived[bar_id] becomes 0 and every warp in m stops waiting (waiting &= ~m). Otherwise arrived[bar_id] becomes m and warp wid waits (its waiting bit becomes 1).

blocks.name: g_tensor_unit
blocks.description: Tensor unit. Lane i of a 128-bit bus is bits 32i+31..32i (four lanes). For each of the 4 warps, a 4 x 4 accumulator ACC of 32-bit values (lane i owns row i). is_t = valid & (unit is TENSOR). Outputs, combinational: err = is_t & (tmask is not 1111); lane i of ld_y = ACC[wid][i][c] where c = lane i of a, bits 1:0 (whatever the operation). On each rising edge: when rst or clear_all is 1, every accumulator becomes 0. Otherwise when advance & is_t & !err, by tensor_op: MMA_I8: ACC[wid][i][j] += the sum over k = 0..3 of A[i][k] * B[k][j] (32-bit wrapping), where A[i][k] is byte k (bits 8k+7..8k) of lane i of a and B[k][j] is byte k of lane j of b, both signed 8-bit; this is one 4 x 4 x 4 multiply-accumulate per instruction (64 products). MMA_LD: nothing changes. MMA_ST: ACC[wid][i][c] = lane i of a for every lane i, where c = lane i of b, bits 1:0. MMA_ZERO: every entry of ACC[wid] becomes 0. Exact indexing, to avoid transposing: A[i][k] = byte k of lane i of a = a[32*i + 8*k + 7 : 32*i + 8*k] (row i of A comes from lane i of a); B[k][j] = byte k of lane j of b = b[32*j + 8*k + 7 : 32*j + 8*k] (column j of B comes from lane j of b: the lane picks the column j and the byte picks k, never the other way round). Each product A[i][k] * B[k][j] is a SIGNED 8-bit by signed 8-bit product (a signed 16-bit value), sign-extended to 32 bits before it is added; the four products and the old ACC[wid][i][j] are added as 32-bit two's-complement values (wrapping). ACC entry (wid, i, j) is element 16*wid + 4*i + j of the flat array. In MMA_LD / ld_y and MMA_ST the column c of lane i is a[32*i + 1 : 32*i] and b[32*i + 1 : 32*i] respectively. Worked example (after MMA_ZERO, one MMA_I8, wid 0, tmask 1111): a = {lane3: 0, lane2: 32'h000000FF, lane1: 32'h00000002, lane0: 32'h0302FF01} (lane 0 holds A[0][0..3] = 1, -1, 2, 3); b = {lane3: 0, lane2: 0, lane1: 32'h01010101, lane0: 32'h07FA0504} (lane 0 holds B[0..3][0] = 4, 5, -6, 7; lane 1 holds B[0..3][1] = 1, 1, 1, 1). Then ACC[0][0][0] = 1*4 + (-1)*5 + 2*(-6) + 3*7 = 8; ACC[0][0][1] = 1 - 1 + 2 + 3 = 5; ACC[0][1][0] = 2*4 = 8; ACC[0][1][1] = 2*1 = 2; ACC[0][2][0] = -1*4 = -4 = 32'hFFFFFFFC; ACC[0][2][1] = -1 = 32'hFFFFFFFF; every other entry is 0. Implementation note: hold the 64 accumulator entries as a flat 1-D array or as separate registers (no multi-dimensional arrays), so that every simulator reads them correctly.

Any other address: y = 0, and err = 1 when valid is 1 and unit is CSR (err is 0 in every other case).
